content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To take up hiking, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Purchase a high-quality topographic map (20 minutes)
Step 2. Download an offline GPS navigation app (10 minutes)
Step 3. Research local trail difficulty ratings (2 hours)
Step 4. Visit a local outdoor outfitter store (1 hour)
Step 5. Break in new hiking boots on a treadmill (3 days)
Step 6. Look up weather patterns for the mountain range (30 minutes)
Step 7. Try on different brands of moisture-wicking socks (45 minutes)
Step 8. Select a lightweight daypack (30 minutes)
Step 9. Compare different brands of trekking poles (1 hour)
Step 10. Print out a physical copy of the emergency contact list (5 minutes)
Step 11. Pack a basic first-aid kit with bandages and antiseptic (20 minutes)
Step 12. Buy a reusable 2-liter water bladder (15 minutes)
Step 13. Fill the water bladder and check for leaks (5 minutes)
Step 14. Watch a video on how to tie specialized hiking knots (15 minutes)
Step 15. Read a guide on Leave No Trace principles (1 hour)
Step 16. Purchase a compact multi-tool (20 minutes)
Step 17. Buy a lightweight emergency bivy sack (10 minutes)
Step 18. Check the expiration dates on sunblock and lip balm (5 minutes)
Step 19. Attend an introductory "Hiking 101" seminar (3 hours)
Step 20. Study a manual on local flora and fauna (2 hours)
Step 21. Practice using trekking poles in the backyard (30 minutes)
Step 22. Mark the intended trail route on the paper map (30 minutes)
Step 23. Test the weight distribution of the packed bag (15 minutes)
Step 24. Look up the elevation gain of the chosen peak (15 minutes)
Step 25. Purchase a reliable compass (25 minutes)
Step 26. Buy a breathable waterproof shell jacket (40 minutes)
Step 27. Pack extra layers of synthetic clothing (10 minutes)
Step 28. Learn how to signal for help using a mirror (30 minutes)
Step 29. Set up a shared digital folder for trip photos (10 minutes)
Step 30. Check the final weather forecast 24 hours before (10 minutes)
Step 31. Buy a high-intensity LED headlamp (20 minutes)
Step 32. Apply a waterproof treatment to the hiking boots (12 hours)
Step 33. Adjust the backpack straps for a custom fit (10 minutes)
Step 34. Calculate the estimated time of arrival at the summit (20 minutes)
Step 35. Prepare a high-protein trail mix (30 minutes)
Step 36. Consult with a seasoned hiker for advice (1 hour)
Step 37. Charge the external battery pack (4 hours)
Step 38. Read reviews of different hiking trails online (2 hours)
Step 39. Purchase electrolyte replacement tablets (10 minutes)
Step 40. Set a budget for all hiking equipment (30 minutes)
Step 41. Learn basic wilderness first aid techniques (8 hours)
Step 42. Buy a pair of durable gaiters (15 minutes)
Step 43. Pack the bag with all essential gear (20 minutes)
Step 44. Perform a final weight check of the backpack (5 minutes)
Step 45. Tell a friend the expected return time (5 minutes)
Step 46. Visit a podiatrist for a foot health checkup (45 minutes)
Step 47. Purchase a whistle for emergency signaling (5 minutes)
Step 48. Cut moleskin patches for blister prevention (10 minutes)
Step 49. Pack a lightweight rain poncho (5 minutes)
Step 50. Buy a book on identifying animal tracks (1 hour)
Step 51. Study the signs of altitude sickness (1 hour)
Step 52. Buy a bear-proof food container (20 minutes)
Step 53. Purchase a small bottle of biodegradable soap (5 minutes)
Step 54. Join a local hiking social media group (15 minutes)
Step 55. Purchase a broad-brimmed sun hat (15 minutes)
Step 56. Take a basic navigation class (4 hours)
Step 57. Pack a high-calorie lunch (15 minutes)
Step 58. Read a blog post about essential hiking gear (30 minutes)
Step 59. Buy spare lithium batteries for the headlamp (10 minutes)
Step 60. Install a topographic map layer on the phone (20 minutes)
Step 61. Take a physical fitness assessment (1 hour)
Step 62. Choose a specific date for the first hike (10 minutes)
Step 63. Purchase a pair of UV-protection sunglasses (20 minutes)
Step 64. Buy a durable pair of hiking trousers (30 minutes)
Step 65. Pack a lightweight trowel for waste (5 minutes)
Step 66. Purchase a variety of energy bars (15 minutes)
Step 67. Research the parking permit requirements for the trailhead (30 minutes)
Step 68. Buy a specialized map waterproof case (10 minutes)
Step 69. Purchase a portable water filter (40 minutes)
Step 70. Learn how to use a compass with a map (2 hours)
